column3: NASB adds “of debts” and “every”; the Hebrew reads “at the end of seven years … a remission.”
“creditor” renders “owner of a loan”; “brother” renders “countryman,” and “the Lord’s remission” uses a lowercase “Lord” for “Yahweh.”
“brother” renders “countryman.”
“poor” renders “needy”; “since” renders “for.”
“listen obediently” renders the doubled verb “surely listen.”
“shall bless” renders the Hebrew perfect “has blessed”; “promised” renders “spoke.”
“brothers” renders “countrymen,” and “towns” renders “gates.”
“freely” and “generously” render the doubled verbs “surely open” and “surely lend.”
“base thought” renders “a word of worthlessness”; “is hostile” renders “is evil.”
“generously” renders the doubled verb “surely give”; “undertakings” renders “undertaking of your hand.”
“freely” renders the doubled verb “surely open”; “needy and poor” reverses the Hebrew order “poor … needy.”
“is sold to you” renders “sells himself to you”; “kinsman” renders “countryman.”
“empty-handed” renders “emptily.”
“furnish him liberally” renders the doubled verb “surely provide”; “wine vat” renders “winepress.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“he fares well with you” renders “it is good for him with you.”
“pierce it through his ear into the door” renders “put it in his ear and in the door”; “servant” renders “slave.”
“seem hard to you” renders “be hard in your eyes”; “with double the service of a hired man” renders “double the hire of a hired man.”
“herd” renders “oxen,” and “flock” renders “sheep.”
“every year” renders “year by year.”
“defect” renders “blemish”; “serious” renders “bad.”
Close to the Hebrew.
